challenge.better_approach: Routing: decide could call build_inspector.answer_fixme itself, so the builder keeps one verb. That is a second write path into the state file from a second machine, and answer_fixme takes no root (it resolves through ticket_file._TICKETS), so the route needs a widening in build_inspector too. The refusal is one component, one branch, and puts the one door in front of the caller. Chosen: refuse and name the door; routing stays available if the refusal proves to cost more round trips than it saves.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That nothing legitimately wants a 'FIXME <k>' outcome line on an outcomes plan. Checked: crossing_fixme counts answers from fixme[n].answer (e1d5) and from decisions[] steps, never from outcomes[], so an outcome stepped 'FIXME k' answers nothing even if the shape let it in.
challenge.prior_art: e1d5f00a2b6c (PROVED, cairn 219247f8a) built the answer door, inspector.answer_fixme, and touched only inspector.py: rehearsal.py's last change is d5a382bb8 (efcb2efe7dd3, 2026-11-16). 4be9d02c71a6 put the shape check into decide, which is why the claimless append now refuses rather than lands. 70f91244f3c0 made writes_to/reads required on a shaped plan. None covers FIXME on an outcomes plan.
challenge.real_collision: None exclusive. decide's docstring promises 'A FIXME <k> with no live line ... appends a new line'; on an outcomes plan that promise is what the shape check already forbids, so the docstring is narrowed in the same act, a distinction recorded rather than a conflict.

answers.falsifier: RED if decide(..., step='FIXME 1', writes_to, reads) on an outcomes-plan ticket with a fixme list in a scratch commons either writes the ticket, or refuses without naming --answer-fixme; RED if the same call on a decisions plan stops appending its FIXME line. Horizon: the next kick-back on a shaped ticket is answered without a peer round trip.
answers.from_idea: none, because the gap was measured live on ticket dda0e72b9c67 (commons 8cf95f0c, three refusals) and reproduced on cairn main efbeeb267 in a scratch commons by akiendelllinux:/tmp/claude-1000/-home-akien-dev-src-cairn/546bccde-fde2-48b2-9435-eaf9605f128f/scratchpad/decide_repro.sh
answers.how: In rehearsal.decide, when lines_key(doc) == 'outcomes' and the step is 'FIXME <k>' with no live line at that step, raise Refused naming `python3 cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py --answer-fixme <id> <k> "<text>" --by <who>`, nothing written. A decisions plan and the D<n> / unlisted steps are unchanged. Red-first proof in cairn/machines/rehearsal/proofs/ over a scratch commons.
answers.traces_to: Law 1 (the resolver is spent on the novel): the builder re-derived which door answers a FIXME on a shaped plan, and the door it found pointed it the wrong way. Also Law 7: the refusal it gave ('outcomes[3] has no claim') named a symptom of its own write, not the caller's mistake.
answers.what: On an outcomes-shaped plan, `cairn rehearse <id> --decide "FIXME <k>"` refuses before anything is built, naming the door that does answer a kick-back (inspector.py --answer-fixme <id> <k>), instead of appending a claimless outcome that the cast shape check then refuses.

bullets.text: Measured: rehearse --decide 'FIXME 1' on dda0's outcomes plan, on main efbeeb267 after e1d5 PROVED, still refuses 'outcomes[3] has no claim', with the ticket bytes unchanged. e1d5 did not touch rehearsal.py.
The refusal named its own write's symptom, not the caller's error: a builder reading it reads 'my plan is wrong', which is how dda0 spent one peer round trip.

title: On an outcomes-shaped plan, `cairn rehearse <id> --decide "FIXME <k>"` refuses before anything is built, naming the door
